entries.title: US Commerce Dept. orders Anthropic to pull Fable 5 and Mythos 5 offline worldwide
entries.why_it_matters: A national government forced a frontier lab to yank live models globally, then reversed course 18 days later. It's the clearest sign yet that AI models are now treated as export-controlled, geopolitically sensitive assets — not just products.

entries.title: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, the world's largest open-weight model
entries.why_it_matters: The largest open-weight model in existence now comes from outside the usual US labs. It resets what "open source frontier model" means and pressures every closed lab's pricing.

entries.title: Eli Lilly brings LillyPod online — pharma's most powerful AI supercomputer
entries.why_it_matters: Traditional wet labs test ~2,000 molecular hypotheses a year; LillyPod can simulate billions in parallel. This is AI compute translating directly into drug-discovery speed, not just chatbot quality.

entries.title: GPT-Live-1 becomes OpenAI's default voice model for Go, Plus, and Pro
entries.why_it_matters: Voice moves from a bolt-on feature to the default interaction mode for hundreds of millions of users overnight.

entries.title: Ames Laboratory's DuctGPT discovers rare-earth-free permanent magnets
entries.why_it_matters: A physics-trained model invented new, cheaper-to-source materials while accounting for production cost — a real case of AI doing original materials-science discovery, not just prediction.

entries.title: GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, Muse Spark 1.1, and Claude Sonnet 5 all ship within days of each other
entries.why_it_matters: Four frontier labs released flagship models in the same week, triggering a price war that's pushing inference costs to record lows. The competitive dynamic is now the story — not any single model.

entries.title: DeepMind's math-reasoning model scores top 1% on IMO problems
entries.why_it_matters: International Mathematical Olympiad problems are among the hardest math competition problems given to humans. Top-1% performance is a genuine reasoning milestone, not a benchmark-gaming one.

entries.title: "Selective activation sparsity" lets small models match 3x-larger ones
entries.why_it_matters: If a model can only activate the parameters relevant to a given task, it needs far less compute to run at the same quality — a real lever on inference cost and on-device AI, not an incremental tweak.
